decisions.answer: One editor — schedule fields sit in the report editor alongside coverage, format and recipients
decisions.decision: Is the schedule set inside the report editor, or in a separate step after the report is defined?
options: One editor — schedule fields sit in the report editor alongside coverage, format and recipients
Two steps — define the report first, then set its schedule in a separate screen or panel
decisions.recommended: One editor — schedule fields sit in the report editor alongside coverage, format and recipients

decisions.answer: Opens the full report editor with the source dashboard pre-chosen
decisions.decision: Does the dashboard entry point ("make a report from this") open the full setup page, or a short form?
options: Opens the full report editor with the source dashboard pre-chosen
Opens a short inline form with only the minimum fields, expandable to the full editor
decisions.recommended: Opens the full report editor with the source dashboard pre-chosen

decisions.answer: A scrolling list of rows, one address per row, with the inside/outside marker and a remove action per row
decisions.decision: What does the recipient list look like at twenty addresses?
options: Chips in a wrapping field, with overflow collapsed behind a "+N more" control
A scrolling list of rows, one address per row, with the inside/outside marker and a remove action per row
A compact summary that opens a full-screen or panel recipient manager
decisions.recommended: A scrolling list of rows, one address per row, with the inside/outside marker and a remove action per row

decisions.answer: Per report — history is reached from a report and scoped to it
decisions.decision: Does run history sit on each report, or in one place for all of them?
options: Per report — history is reached from a report and scoped to it
One module-wide history, filterable by report
Both — a module-wide view, and a per-report view filtered from it
decisions.recommended: Per report — history is reached from a report and scoped to it

decisions.answer: A fixed set: daily, weekly, monthly
decisions.decision: Which repeat intervals does the schedule offer?
options: A fixed set: daily, weekly, monthly
A fixed set plus quarterly and yearly
An arbitrary interval builder (every N days/weeks/months)
decisions.recommended: A fixed set: daily, weekly, monthly

decisions.answer: Read-only — a Technician may see system reports and read run history, but may not create, share or schedule
decisions.decision: Does a Technician use this module at all? Three cells of the PRD permission table are left [NEEDS INPUT]: see system reports, create a private report, and read run history.
options: No — a Technician sees no part of this module; every reporting control is hidden for them
Read-only — a Technician may see system reports and read run history, but may not create, share or schedule
Yes, like an Engineer for their own reports — see system reports, create private reports, read their own run history
decisions.recommended: Read-only — a Technician may see system reports and read run history, but may not create, share or schedule

decisions.answer: Yes, gated on the send-outside-the-organization privilege, held by Owner and Admin only
decisions.decision: May a report be emailed to an address outside the client's own organization? The PRD leaves three cells of the permission table unfilled pending a leadership answer.
options: Yes, gated on the "send outside the organization" privilege, held by Owner and Admin only
Yes, gated on the privilege, and Engineers may hold it too
No — recipients must be inside the client's domain in this release
decisions.recommended: Yes, gated on the "send outside the organization" privilege, held by Owner and Admin only

decisions.answer: WCAG 2.2 AA across the screen surfaces only; the PDF and email are out of scope for this release
decisions.decision: What accessibility bar does this module have to meet? The ANNEX records it as [NEEDS INPUT] — "no requirement was given, and none is invented."
options: WCAG 2.2 AA across the four screen surfaces, with the PDF meeting tagged-PDF basics
WCAG 2.2 AA across the screen surfaces only; the PDF and email are out of scope for this release
Match whatever bar the Admin Module and dashboard builders were held to, whatever that turns out to be
No stated bar in this release
decisions.recommended: WCAG 2.2 AA across the screen surfaces only; the PDF and email are out of scope for this release

decisions.answer: Yes — a diagram panel contributes the series values, so a chart-only dashboard still produces a usable workbook
decisions.decision: Should a diagram-only dashboard exported to Excel carry the values behind its charts? The PRD proposes yes (Requirement 6) and marks it Architect-proposed — confirm.
options: Yes — a diagram panel contributes the series values, so a chart-only dashboard still produces a usable workbook
No — Excel export carries only table panels; a chart-only dashboard produces an empty-stated workbook
decisions.recommended: Yes — a diagram panel contributes the series values, so a chart-only dashboard still produces a usable workbook

decisions.answer: The client's own wording — do not name it in the design; it maps onto existing roles
decisions.decision: Is "Technical Office" a user the design should name, or the client's own word for a team that maps onto roles Sand already has?
options: The client's own wording — do not name it in the design; it maps onto existing roles
A distinct user the personas and screens should name explicitly
decisions.recommended: The client's own wording — do not name it in the design; it maps onto existing roles

decisions.answer: No ceiling shown up front — it surfaces only as a failed run with a stated reason in run history
decisions.decision: What is the attachment size ceiling, and how is it communicated in the editor before a run fails?
options: A stated ceiling shown in the editor as guidance while recipients and coverage are chosen
No ceiling shown up front — it surfaces only as a failed run with a stated reason in the run history
A stated ceiling plus a pre-flight warning when the chosen coverage is likely to exceed it
decisions.recommended: No ceiling shown up front — it surfaces only as a failed run with a stated reason in the run history

decisions.answer: Files are retained but not retrievable from the UI in this release — run history references them without offering them
decisions.decision: How long is a generated file kept, and does the run history let a person retrieve it?
options: Files are retrievable from run history for a stated retention period shown on the run row
Files are retained but not retrievable from the UI in this release — run history references them without offering them
No retention stated; run history records the file reference only
decisions.recommended: Files are retained but not retrievable from the UI in this release — run history references them without offering them

decisions.answer: Run on the last day of any month that is shorter than the start day
decisions.decision: With monthly intervals settled, what does a monthly schedule do in a month that is too short — a report started on the 29th, 30th or 31st?
options: Run on the last day of any month that is shorter than the start day
Skip the month entirely and run at the next month that has that day
Clamp the choosable start day to 1–28 so the case cannot arise
decisions.recommended: Run on the last day of any month that is shorter than the start day

decisions.answer: No UI route at all — retrieval is a support or engineering action, and the run row says so
decisions.decision: Gate 1 decided generated files are retained but not retrievable from the UI. REQ-58 requires a too-large file to be retained "so somebody can retrieve it" — by what route, then?
options: No UI route at all — retrieval is a support/engineering action, and the run row says so
A single exception: the too-large-file failure row offers the file, nothing else does
Drop the retrieval promise from REQ-58 — the file is retained for diagnosis only, and the run row promises nothing
decisions.recommended: No UI route at all — retrieval is a support/engineering action, and the run row says so
